title: A session-time lore producer leaves cache generation directories without the owner write bit, so the owner cannot delete the checkout
description: FILED, NOT BUILT. Relayed by team-lead 2026-10-13; opum-doc ruled under DEC-183 (g) that this rides behind the v0.14.0 pair (constitution Article 3), so it is not in LCLI-714. FINDING: a session-time lore producer writes cache generation directories without the u+w bit inside whatever checkout a Claude session starts in, and the owner then cannot delete that checkout. MEASURED 2026-10-13 by opum-desktop in its DEC-183 reader worktree .claude/worktrees/review-36 (a relayed measurement, not re-resolved here): .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations/8ab4c4c5.../ has mode dr-xr-xr-x and holds projection.lbdb (r--r--r--) and index.json (r--------). It was created at 14:26 local by the reader session itself; nothing ran in the worktree before the spawn. git worktree remove then failed with Permission denied after partially deleting the tree; the same happened earlier with review-28 and review-31. opum-workflow 0.15.8 session-start.sh and session-end.sh do not invoke lore, so the opum-lore plugin session module (or a lore CLI call it makes) is the likely producer, UNVERIFIED. QUESTIONS THIS TASK ANSWERS: (1) which code path produces the generation directories at session time, and with what modes; (2) are the read-only bits deliberate (immutable generations)? PENDING DESIGN QUESTION, for opum-doc: do not pick a fix. Candidate (a): generations stay read-only and lore exposes a supported cleanup. Candidate (b): a reviewer session skips the cache. Related prior knowledge: ladybug directories are read-only in test fixtures and need chmod before rm (see the fixture scaffolding note).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The code path that creates a generation directory at session time is identified, with the modes it sets, and the finding is recorded on this task
The task records whether the read-only modes are deliberate, citing the code or ADR that says so
opum-doc's design ruling between the supported-cleanup arm and the reviewer-skips-cache arm is recorded before any code changes
Whichever arm is ruled, a checkout whose session created a generation can be removed by its owner with git worktree remove, shown by a reproduction before and after

implementationNotes: DEC-281 (a1), ODOC-608 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T22:49:37Z): option C was reversed. Generation directories stay 0555 and the inspector's immutability check stays as written, because C would have changed a deliberate integrity check. The incident's cause is already fixed, since LCLI-705 gates the pane producer from 0.14.0, and the review-36 observation of 2026-10-13 predates the 0.14.0 bump of 2026-10-19, so it ran 0.13.x or older. The remaining case has a supported path, lore cache clear (LCLI-740), shipping in the next pair release, after which DEC-208's worktree hold lifts. DEC-281 (a2), ODOC-608, opum-ai/opum-doc#1776 (2026-11-18T22:51:24Z): LCLI-718 is REOPENED on the specimen below. lore-cli keeps this record OPEN and did not close it. Next is a measurement only: name the producer in review worktrees (the assignment prepare's lore agent context, the tracker-write hook's lore check, or another caller), and report it. Then opum-doc rules the shape: either C (directory 0755, immutability checked on the files, dropping the line-813 directory test) or stopping that caller from writing a cache in a review worktree. Until then the inspector check stays as it is. SPECIMEN: .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations in opum-desktop worktree review-125-3ae5ee2, created 2026-10-21 11:49. Modes measured: generations/ 0700, the generation directory 0555, index.json 0400, projection.lbdb 0444. Its control manifest records loreVersion 0.14.1 and exporterVersion 0.14.1, so the defect reproduced on a 0.14.0-or-later lore, which matches (a2)'s concern. MEASUREMENTS: the publish path is src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts lines 330, 371 and 373, reached through reconcileLadybugProjection (line 174) from any retrieval command; the read-only bits are deliberate because the inspector classifies a writable generation as corrupt (lines 813-828). CARRY FROM LCLI-724 (closed as a duplicate of this record): (1) when git worktree remove fails with Permission denied, git worktree list no longer shows the path, so the leftover reads as clutter rather than as the residue of a command that half-succeeded; (2) the DEC-158 ownership guard refuses a session any write inside a worktree path, so even a session that knows about the leftover cannot chmod or rm it by hand. STATUS: open pending the producer measurement; the shape is not ruled (C or stop the caller). This is a ruling note, not activity (grooming ruling D2).
